note:
The "keep_out_violations: ['cabinet']" refusals come from a keep-out box the orchestrator added for this task (task
yaml `keep_out`): no gripper point may be more than 1 cm behind the cabinet's front plane, anywhere across the cabinet's
width (t from -0.155 to -0.005 m along the front) and up to 0.305 m above the table. The model's gripper points are the
fingertips plus a 45 mm-radius cylinder around the tool axis from the flange to the knuckles (`rlpj.robot.sim.gripper_points`).
So with the gripper vertical, the tool axis has to stay about 5.5 cm in front of the front plane while the gripper body
is at cabinet height; a tilted gripper (pointing forward and down at the pull) keeps the body out of the box. Check your
segments offline with `rlpj.robot.sim.check` (it uses the same box) before a real run. The box stays: it keeps the
arm off the cabinet.

report:
The reset program can't pull the drawer out. The pin pull is the only handle, and within the current keep-out box the fingers can reach only its last ~5 mm.

Measured (inputs for your decision):
- I photographed the pin from 3 wrist poses (attempts 9-10, no contact) and triangulated it, with ~1 mm residuals. The pin is ~12 mm in diameter and its axis is ~0.028 m above the table at t = -0.088. It runs from 0.011 m BEHIND the task yaml front plane (normal . xy = 0.5226) to about the plane itself. So the real drawer face is ~1.1 cm behind fixtures.cabinet.front_offset.
- Contact check: in attempt 13 the model put the leading finger edge 9 mm behind the yaml plane. Peak tool force was 3.5 N, so no contact. The face really is further back than the yaml says.
- The keep-out box starts 1 cm behind the yaml plane, so in practice it sits at the real face. A gripper tilted 50 deg (more folds joint 3 to its limit) can then cover only the pin's last ~5 mm, its rounded end. Attempts 12 and 13: the pin was visibly between the fingers, and the gripper closed to 99.1 on nothing both times.

Request (one of):
(a) Move the cabinet front plane and the keep-out box 1 cm deeper, to match the real face: front_offset 0.5226 -> 0.5326, keep_out cabinet center shifted by +0.010*[0.9282, 0.3722], i.e. [0.6727, 0.1835, 0.134]. The box would still stay 1 cm behind the real front.
(b) Or tell me the box must stay as it is. Then the pin can't be grasped and the drawer has to be pulled out by hand before each reset. The rest of the program (pick from the table, place at the target, verify) still works from a table start state, but it is untested on hardware.
